item.text: {"summary":"Correct fractional-second scaling between Abseil time ticks and CCTZ femtoseconds.","explanation":"The formatting assertions use a time with 6 ms, 7 μs, and 8 ns, then expect `%E3S`, `%E6S`, `%E9S`, `%E*S`, and `%E15S` to preserve those fractions. `Split()` currently multiplies the low duration part by 1,000,000, producing four times the expected fraction; Abseil’s low part is in quarter-nanosecond ticks, so each tick corresponds to 250,000 femtoseconds. The parse assertions for `%E*S` inputs `0.2147483647`, `0.2147483648`, and a longer input expect quarter-nanosecond precision, including a half-nanosecond result. `Join()` currently divides by 1,000,000 and loses that precision; dividing by 250,000 converts the parsed femtoseconds back to Abseil ticks. Updating both directions restores the interchange contract.","edits":[{"path":"absl/time/format.cc","old":"  const auto fem = cctz::detail::femtoseconds(rep_lo * (1000 * 1000));","new":"  const auto fem = cctz::detail::femtoseconds(rep_lo * 250000);"},{"path":"absl/time/format.cc","old":"  const uint32_t rep_lo =\n      static_cast<uint32_t>(parts.fem.count() / (1000 * 1000));","new":"  const uint32_t rep_lo =\n      static_cast<uint32_t>(parts.fem.count() / 250000);"}]}
